title: REVOLUTION MEN'S LEAGUE | WEEK 1 RECAP
content: Week 1 was a scoring bonanza to open the Revolution Men's Fall League. Kyle Haley torched the twine for 35 points as Orange sprinted past Gray; Matt Spear matched that number to push Pink past Green in overtime; Cam Perta buried ten trey balls in Red's rout of Blue; and White cruised past Black even with Matt Riordan pouring in 31 on the other side. Let's get into the action.

games.text: White wasted no time announcing themselves. Asko Mostarlic fueled the early offense with his perimeter shooting, Adam Gawrys patrolled the glass, and Aaron West kept the offense honest around the rim. Black hung around thanks to Matt Riordan. He relentlessly drove to the cup, but the supporting cast couldn't find the range, so White carried a five-point edge into the locker room. Halftime: White 36, Black 31. Black came out swinging after the break. Riordan kept the pressure on, finishing 14-of-26 from the field with 12 rebounds and 3 blocks, while Drew Fisher crashed the boards, and Brody Snow chipped in timely scoring. Black's problem was the arc: the team finished just 2-of-24 from three-point range. Meanwhile, White had Joe Ruggles knock down four triples, which helped White outscore Black 43-24 after the break. White took the opener, 79-55.

performers.White: Asko Mostarlic — 24 pts, 11 reb, 6 ast, 2 stl; Joe Ruggles — 14 pts, 10 reb, 4 ast; Adam Gawrys — 12 pts, 14 reb, 1 ast
performers.Black: Matt Riordan — 31 pts, 12 reb, 3 ast, 3 blk; Brody Snow — 10 pts, 5 reb, 1 ast, 1 stl; Aiden Brown — 8 pts, 4 reb, 2 ast

games.text: Orange treated the opening half like a track meet. Kyle Haley set the tone from long range, Edo Semic supplied steady scoring, and Kerry Lyons dominated the glass to give Orange extra possessions. Carter Beeman and Brandon Boyer also contributed at both ends. Gray managed just 24 points in the first half, while Orange built a commanding cushion. Halftime: Orange 48, Gray 24. Gray steadied itself after the break. Cory Chaplin kept launching from deep, Jeromy Anderson finished a perfect 6-for-6 from the field, and Jimmy Warden pressured the defense with strong drives. Gray matched Orange stride for stride, 40-40 over the final half, but the halftime hole proved too deep to climb out of. Orange cruised, 88-64.

performers.Orange: Kyle Haley — 35 pts, 7 reb, 3 ast, 3 stl; Edo Semic — 17 pts; Kerry Lyons — 12 pts, 14 reb, 3 ast
performers.Gray: Cory Chaplin — 24 pts, 8 reb, 2 ast, 2 stl; Jimmy Warden — 15 pts, 6 reb, 3 ast, 1 stl; Jeromy Anderson — 13 pts, 8 reb

games.text: Green and Pink traded haymakers in the opening half. Fab Anthony carried the load for Green, hunting shots and drawing contact, while Kenny Black and Peter Lindholm added scoring and rebounding support. Pink countered with Dylan Pratico's shooting touch and Matt Spear's aggressiveness attacking the rim. Neither side could gain an edge, and the teams walked off level. Halftime: Green 37, Pink 37. The tug-of-war continued after the break. Spear kept punishing Green at the free-throw line, and Liam Walsh added steady scoring, while Anthony refused to let Green fade. Both teams scored 31 in the second half, which sent regulation to a 68-68 finish. In the extra period, Pink outscored Green 7-2 to seal it. The final score was 75-70, Pink.

performers.Green: Fab Anthony — 32 pts, 13 reb, 2 ast, 1 stl; Kenny Black — 11 pts, 10 reb; Peter Lindholm — 11 pts, 6 reb
performers.Pink: Matt Spear — 35 pts, 7 reb, 2 ast, 1 blk, 3 stl; Dylan Pratico — 13 pts, 6 reb, 1 ast; Liam Walsh — 13 pts, 3 reb, 2 ast

games.text: Red arrived with its shooting touch dialed in. Cam Perta fired from deep and connected on 10 of 17 three-point attempts, and Drew Pelkey added steady scoring punch. Logan Letourneau controlled the boards, while Dylan Mackie orchestrated the offense. Blue leaned on John Helsel inside, but the offense could not keep pace as Red opened a 42-29 lead. Halftime: Red 42, Blue 29. Blue regrouped after the break. Kyle Picard led the charge with 18 points, while Will Ewald and Will Oboh each finished with 13, and Ewald even grabbed 12 rebounds. Blue trimmed the deficit, but Red answered every push and outscored Blue 36-28 in the second half to keep the gap intact. Red closed out the morning with a 78-57 win.
